title: Toolkit CPT dynamic tags and runtime field lookup
purpose: Turn Toolkit-managed CPT definitions into usable Elementor field bindings for the Filter Controller.
objective: Expose managed meta/taxonomy fields in Elementor dynamic tags and let the runtime read public Toolkit meta values without requiring every field to be printed in the DOM.
scope_boundary: In scope: field catalog, Elementor dynamic tag registration, serialized key compatibility, public Toolkit meta enrichment, and implementation documentation. Out of scope: per-filter visual redesign, sort-field builder, arbitrary third-party meta discovery, and Elementor UI deep QA.
entry_condition: TASK-FC-045 has established the field binding resolver and normalized source contract.
exit_condition: TASK-FC-046 is implemented, validated, documented, committed, and pushed in the plugin repository.
completion_criteria: Toolkit field options are sourced from CptManager definitions.
The Elementor tag registers under a Toolkit group and returns a sanitized field key.
FieldBindingResolver can resolve a serialized Toolkit dynamic tag payload.
FilterResolver can enrich public post items with Toolkit meta values for show_in_rest fields.

phases.title: Catalog
phases.purpose: Create a reusable catalog of public Toolkit field options and runtime-readable meta keys.

phases.title: Elementor tag
phases.purpose: Register the Toolkit dynamic tag group and field-key tag through the Elementor manager.

phases.title: Runtime lookup
phases.purpose: Allow the filter resolver to read public Toolkit meta values for public posts.

phases.title: Verification
phases.purpose: Validate schemas, syntax, Elementor registration, resolver compatibility, and git hygiene.

acceptance_criteria: No Elementor Pro-only class is required.
No arbitrary meta key lookup is introduced.
No existing manual field-binding behavior is removed.
The implementation remains PSR-4 and module-scoped.
verification: PHP lint passes for changed PHP files.
stop_conditions: The implementation starts redesigning filter visuals.
The runtime requires exposing private or arbitrary post meta.
The tag cannot register through Elementor's local dynamic tag manager API.
